answer: I would like to talk about a trip I made to Kolkata, in India, a couple of years ago, which left a lasting impression on me. I went during the winter with two friends from university, and we spent about five days there. It is an old, historic city, and what struck me immediately was its wonderful sense of character. The streets were [[bustling]] with activity, full of markets, trams and street food that smelled incredible. What I loved most was the blend of old and new; grand colonial buildings stood alongside modern shops, creating a genuinely [[atmospheric]] feel. I spent my days exploring museums and wandering through the older neighbourhoods, which felt almost [[timeless]]. We also rode one of the old trams, which rattled along at a wonderfully slow pace. We visited the Victoria Memorial, and I spent a whole afternoon on College Street, which is lined with second-hand bookshops, so as a keen reader I was completely [[in my element]]. The people were remarkably friendly and always happy to point me in the right direction, and since so many of them speak Bengali, I never felt like a complete outsider. Of course, it was crowded and chaotic at times, but that energy was part of its charm. Honestly, I found the whole experience genuinely [[invigorating]], and it gave me a real appreciation for the city's rich cultural heritage. In a way it also felt strangely familiar, because we share so much history, language and food. I would go back without hesitation, ideally for longer next time.

followUps.q: Would you like to go back to Kolkata?
followUps.answer: Yes, definitely. Next time I would like to stay longer and explore some of the smaller neighbourhoods and old cafés. I would also love to go during Durga Puja, when the whole city is beautifully lit up.

followUps.q: Do you prefer visiting cities or the countryside?
followUps.answer: It depends on my mood, really. Cities are exciting for a few days, but I get tired of the noise quite quickly, so for a proper rest I would usually choose the countryside.
